name: GUSINSKY
description: Concurred, argued that law enforcement officers qualify as victims under Marsy's Law and are entitled to request redaction of their names and initials from public filings, but a balancing test is required against other constitutional rights.

name: SALTER, Justice
description: Concurred specially, noting the unusual procedural posture of the habeas appeal and agreeing to reach the merits despite potential procedural default issues not litigated by the parties.

name: DEVANEY, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that E.H. did not waive her constitutional right to privacy and that the Waldners' subpoena failed to meet the specificity requirements of the Nixon test, thus the circuit court erred in denying the motion to quash.

name: SALTER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Article III, § 12 does not prohibit all contracts between legislators and the State, overruling prior precedent that equated general appropriation with authorization for specific contracts.

name: KERN, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the majority opinion wrongly overrules decades of established precedent by exempting general appropriations from Article III, § 12, and that this approach disregards constitutional text and may not provide clarity.

name: SALTER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Article III, § 12 does not prohibit all contracts between legislators and the State, overruling Asphalt Surfacing and Pitts because general appropriation bills only allocate money and do not authorize specific contracts for ordinary expenses.

name: KERN, Justice
description: Dissented in part and concurred in part, argued that the majority wrongly overrules decades of precedent by exempting general appropriations from Article III, § 12, and that "any law" includes general appropriations, but joined the holding that Article III, § 12 applies to laws passed during a legislator's term.

name: SALTER, Justice
description: Concurred specially, arguing that while Amendment A violated the single-subject rule, the court should leave open the question of whether such a violation always renders an entire amendment void, suggesting separability might be appropriate in some cases.

name: MYREN, Justice
description: Dissented in part, arguing that Amendment A contained a single subject because its propositions were incidental to and necessarily connected with the comprehensive plan for legalizing, regulating, and taxing marijuana and related substances, and therefore did not violate Article XXIII, § 1.

name: JENSEN, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, delivering the majority opinion that dismissed the inverse condemnation and excessive force claims, but allowed the unlawful entry claim to proceed.

name: KERN, Justice
description: Concurred with the majority on the inverse condemnation and unlawful entry claims, but dissented on the dismissal of the excessive force claim, arguing it should proceed to trial.

name: SALTER, Justice
description: Concurred with the majority opinion on all issues.

name: DEVANEY, Justice
description: Concurred with the majority on the inverse condemnation and unlawful entry claims, but dissented on the dismissal of the excessive force claim.

name: GILBERTSON, Retired Chief Justice
description: Dissented on the unlawful entry claim, arguing the circuit court should have decided qualified immunity as a matter of law, and concurred in the result on the inverse condemnation and excessive force claims.

name: MYREN, Justice
description: Did not participate in the case.
